text: Sanborn spoke of matrix codes and then going back to the table. A Hill cipher is a matrix code; here a Hill matrix of size 2 to 4 is joined to a repeating key of 1 to 26 letters, in either order, which comes to one model: message = matrix x carved block + a shift.
Every known letter gives one equation for one row of the matrix and one shift. Solved exactly mod 2 and mod 13, a setting is dead if the equations contradict or the matrix cannot be undone.
Nothing is alive on K4 or on ten scrambled coppers. 536 settings are dead; 400 stay open where the key is long and the equations too few. A planted text of this kind is recovered.
